scope: Android 10 (API 29) through Android 17 (API 37); AOSP Developer options, Pixel, Samsung One UI, and adb test controls. Desk research only: nothing here was run on a device.
source_note: Curated subset of desk research. Nothing in this catalog was run on a device by ADAPT; confidence is per entry. Privileged entries are left out.

field_notes.commands: read_cmd, write_cmd and restore_cmd are device shell commands. Prefix each with: adb -s SERIAL shell. PKG is an app package name. null means no shell-UID path is known.
field_notes.restore_cmd: SNAPSHOT means: write back the value saved before the change with the same settings put form, or run settings delete TABLE KEY when the key was absent. PROP_EMPTY means: setprop NAME '' (debug.* properties also clear on reboot).
field_notes.min_api: 29 means present at or before API 29 (the scope floor), not introduced in 29.
field_notes.max_api: Last API level where the entry is on the main AOSP Developer options screen or the command works; null means still present in android17-release.
field_notes.needs_reboot: no | yes | poke (system property; running apps see it only after a SystemProperties poke or an app process restart) | app_restart | unknown
field_notes.confidence: high = read in AOSP source or official documentation during this research; medium = AOSP or official knowledge not re-read this session, or official documentation that is incomplete; low = forum, blog or memory only
field_notes.api_levels: 29=10, 30=11, 31=12, 32=12L, 33=13, 34=14, 35=15, 36=16, 37=17. Quarterly platform releases (QPR) do not change the API level and are named in oem_notes.

entries.restore_cmd: setprop both properties back to the saved values (or empty)
entries.oem_notes: Meaningful only on a device already running a 16 KB kernel. Forcing compat off (or fatal on Android 17) makes binaries with 4 KB alignment fail, which is the check Google Play requires for updates targeting Android 15 and higher from 1 February 2027. Any device or emulator with a 16 KB kernel, not only Pixel.

entries.oem_notes: One UI 6.0 and later. Protections: blocks apps from unauthorized sources, blocks commands by USB cable, blocks malware images in messaging apps, blocks non-official software updates. Users and Samsung developer forum staff report that it switches USB debugging off and greys it out. When adb fails on a Samsung device, tell the user to check this first. A community post claims One UI 9 cuts the USB data connection entirely while it is on; not confirmed by Samsung.

entries.ui_name: High contrast text, bold text, colour inversion
entries.mechanism: Settings.Secure high_text_contrast_enabled, font_weight_adjustment (300 = bold, Android 12+), accessibility_display_inversion_enabled
entries.read_cmd: settings get secure high_text_contrast_enabled ; settings get secure font_weight_adjustment ; settings get secure accessibility_display_inversion_enabled
entries.write_cmd: settings put secure high_text_contrast_enabled 1 ; settings put secure font_weight_adjustment 300
entries.oem_notes: Android 16 changed high contrast text to an outline style. Samsung bold font uses its own key.

Recording stops at 180 seconds, has no audio, and does not follow rotation. Secure windows are blank. On Android 15 and later sensitive notifications and password fields are hidden unless aosp.disable_screen_share_protections is on.

entries.default: verify after install, speed-profile after idle maintenance
entries.oem_notes: Makes start-up measurements comparable: -m verify shows the just-installed worst case, speed-profile the steady state (needs a baseline or cloud profile), speed the fully compiled case. --reset returns to the install state.
reset only clears the app's own counters. Reports janky frame percentage and percentile frame times without any developer option being on.

entries.ui_name: Process death and memory pressure for one app
entries.read_cmd: pidof PKG ; dumpsys activity processes PKG
entries.write_cmd: am kill PKG ; am send-trim-memory PKG RUNNING_CRITICAL ; am crash PKG
entries.oem_notes: am kill only works while the app is in the background, which reproduces system-initiated process death and state restoration more faithfully than Don't keep activities. am force-stop is different: it also cancels alarms and jobs. From Android 14 send-trim-memory levels other than background ones are no longer delivered to apps the same way.
